title: Marked dualizing line bundle and contracted-component degrees
statement: Let $T$ be an integral Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $(X,D)$ be a multipointed $T$-curve with smooth generic curve and etale generic marking, and let $f:(Y,E)\to(X,D)$ be a stable $\eta$-modification. There is an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] $\mathcal L=\omega_{Y/T}(E)$, compatible with every base change of $T$. Here $E$ is an effective Cartier divisor, with associated twist as in [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle], and $\omega_{Y/T}$ is the relative dualizing line bundle, equivalently the invertible module locally given, for a regular closed immersion $i:Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf A_T^n$ (locally cut out by a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]), by $\mathcal Ext^{n-1}(i_*\mathcal O_Y,\Omega^n_{\mathbf A_T^n/T})$ restricted to $Y$; sheaf Ext is [def-weil-pbc-sheaf-ext]; these local modules glue canonically, including when $Y\to T$ is nonseparated. For a geometric fibre over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and a proper irreducible component $Z$ of $Y_\Omega$ with normalization $\nu:\bar Z\to Z$, one has $\deg(\nu^*\mathcal L)=2g(\bar Z)-2+n_Z$, where $g(\bar Z)=\dim_\Omega H^1(\bar Z,\mathcal O_{\bar Z})$ and $n_Z$ counts the preimages on $\bar Z$ of the nodal branches of $Y_\Omega$ together with its marked points. Degree is [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. In particular, for every geometric point $z\to X$ and every one-dimensional irreducible component $Z$ of $(Y_z)_{\mathrm{red}}$, the pullback of $\mathcal L$ to its normalization has strictly positive degree. A multipointed curve $(X,D)$ over a scheme $T$ means flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphisms $X\to T$, $D\to T$ of pure relative dimensions $1$, $0$ and a closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; $D$ may be empty and $X$ need not be separated or proper over $T$. It is semistable if every singular point of every geometric fibre has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field, $D\to T$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $D$ lies in the relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For integral $T$ with generic point $\eta$, an $\eta$-modification of multipointed curves is a compatible pair $f_X:X'\to X$, $f_D:D'\to D$ of proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism], each an isomorphism over a schematically dense open and on its generic fibre. A semistable such modification is stable if in each geometric fibre there is no irreducible component isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1$ that is contracted by $f_X$ and meets the union of the marking and the singular points of $X'$ in at most two points. Geometric fibres are [def-weil-geometric-fibre]; dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; the local completion is at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $\Omega[[u,v]]$ denotes the two-variable formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Normalization of an integral component has the meaning of [def-sc-normalization]. Here an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense when $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective.

source.place: §1.2, construction of omega and its base-change and normalization-residue description (a),(b), pp. 2--3; the contracted-subcurve computation in proof of Theorem 1.1, p. 3. Positivity includes the boundary nodes joining a contracted subcurve to its complement.

proof.text: The source $(Y,E)$ is semistable by the definition of a stable modification. Apply [lem-trf-semistable-marked-base-change]: all geometric fibres of $Y/T$ are nodal, $E/T$ is etale and flat of finite presentation, and $E$ lies in the relative smooth locus $U\subset Y$; all these assertions persist under arbitrary base change. Over an algebraically closed field, the etale marking is unramified by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. By [lem-trf-unramified-over-field-local-criterion] each of its local rings is its residue field, equal to the ground field. Thus the marking is reduced with multiplicity one at each of its distinct smooth points. No properness or separatedness of $Y/T$ is being asserted.

source.place: §1.2, multipointed and semistable definitions and property (a).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-nodal-curve-lci-criterion] to each residue-field fibre: the geometric-node condition in its (1) holds by step 1, so each fibre is a local complete intersection. In affine coordinates $R\to S$ around any point of $Y$, finite presentation and flatness are given. The definition [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field] supplies an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of the residue-field fibre containing the point and $a\in A$ with $A_a$ a global complete intersection over the residue field. The fibre of the chosen chart is $\operatorname{Spec}F$, $F=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$; the point has a neighbourhood which is principal in both $\operatorname{Spec}F$ and $\operatorname{Spec}A_a$, say $F_h=(A_a)_b$, and $F_h$ is again a global complete intersection by [lem-weil-pbc-global-complete-intersection-principal-localization]. This is hypothesis (3) of the next lemma. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-syntomic-at-prime-relative-global-complete-intersection] gives a principal neighbourhood of the original point with a relative global complete-intersection presentation $S_g=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$. Its nonempty fibres have dimension $n-c$ by [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection], so $c=n-1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-local-regular-sequence] these equations form a regular sequence at each point along the immersion. We have obtained the local regular closed immersions needed for adjunction.

source.place: §1.2, relative local complete-intersection assertion; Stacks Tags 0C4D, 00SL, 00SY, 00SP, 00SV and 00SA for the cited fibre and regular-sequence criteria.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-flat-lci-canonical-adjunction] with $d=1$ to the presentations just obtained. Its determinant line $K_{Y/T}$ is invertible and, in every such chart $i:Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^n_T$, its pushforward is the sheaf $\mathcal Ext^{n-1}(i_*\mathcal O_Y,\Omega^n_{\mathbf A^n_T/T})$. The canonical transition maps satisfy the cocycle condition on arbitrary overlaps, so their gluing does not require affine intersections or separatedness. Define $\omega_{Y/T}=K_{Y/T}$; its separated-chart relative dualizing description is precisely the one in the statement. The same lemma supplies its canonical arbitrary-base-change isomorphisms, including for non-Noetherian base changes.

source.place: §1.2, local Ext construction and property (a); Stacks Tags 0B6V and 0E2Y.

proof.text: On $U$, the relative smooth locus containing $E$, the closed marking is etale over $T$, hence unramified and flat of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Its structural map is locally quasi-finite by [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-quasi-finite-at-points]. Apply (3)$\Rightarrow$(2) of [lem-pc-cartier-criterion] to the smooth relative curve $U/T$: $E$ is a relative effective Cartier divisor there. On the open complement $Y\setminus E$ its ideal is the unit ideal, and this together with $U$ covers $Y$, so the same local non-zero-divisor condition holds globally. Since $E/T$ is flat by step 1, this is a relative effective Cartier divisor globally by [def-pc-relative-effective-cartier]. The associated module $\mathcal O_Y(E)$ is invertible by [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. Define $\mathcal L=\omega_{Y/T}\otimes\mathcal O_Y(E)$, which is invertible by [lem-pc-tensor-dual-invertible]. For any $T'\to T$, [lem-pc-recd-pullback] identifies the divisor twist after base change with the pullback twist; combine this with step 3 to obtain the asserted base-change identification for $\mathcal L$.

source.place: §1.2, marking is Cartier and definition of the marked dualizing module; Stacks Picard Tag 0B9D and relative Cartier pullback.

proof.text: Fix a geometric fibre $C=Y_\Omega$ and a proper irreducible component $Z$. By step 3 the restriction of $\omega_{Y/T}$ is $K_{C/\Omega}$. Apply [lem-trf-nodal-normalization-adjunction] to $C,Z$: the normalization $\bar Z$ is smooth proper connected and $\nu^*\omega_{Y/T}=\Omega^1_{\bar Z/\Omega}(B_Z)$, with one point in $B_Z$ per ambient nodal branch on this component. Write $M_Z$ for the points above $E_\Omega\cap Z$. These are reduced and disjoint from $B_Z$ by step 1. Since the normalization is an isomorphism near each marked smooth point, pulling its Cartier equation back gives the reduced point equation on $\bar Z$ with multiplicity one. Thus $\nu^*\mathcal L\cong\Omega^1_{\bar Z/\Omega}(B_Z+M_Z)$. The effective divisor $B_Z+M_Z$ is Cartier by [lem-sc-point-cartier], and its number of points is exactly the $n_Z$ in the statement; a self-node contributes two branches.

source.place: §1.2(b), normalization-residue description, and the boundary divisor in Theorem 1.1.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-riemann-roch] to a line bundle $F$ on $\bar Z$. Subtracting its formula $\chi(\mathcal O_{\bar Z})=1-g$ from $\chi(F)=\deg_{\mathrm{class}}F+1-g$ gives $\deg_{\mathrm{Euler}}F=\deg_{\mathrm{class}}F$, so the degree convention in the item agrees with the one in [lem-sc-canonical-degree]. The latter gives $\deg\Omega^1_{\bar Z/\Omega}=2g(\bar Z)-2$. Every point in $B_Z+M_Z$ is $\Omega$-rational. The effective-divisor tensor and point-count formulas of [lem-pc-degree-base-change] therefore yield $\deg\nu^*\mathcal L=(2g(\bar Z)-2)+\#(B_Z+M_Z)=2g(\bar Z)-2+n_Z$. This also covers empty marking or empty branch divisor.

source.place: Theorem 1.1, classical degree computation; Stacks Tag 0BS6 and the cited Picard degree formulas.

proof.text: Let $z:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ be geometric, with induced geometric point of $T$, and let $Z$ be a one-dimensional irreducible component of $(Y_z)_{\mathrm{red}}$. The point $z$ is closed in $X_\Omega$: in any affine neighbourhood its defining $\Omega$-algebra map to $\Omega$ is surjective, so its kernel is maximal; any specialization can be tested in an affine neighbourhood containing it and $z$. The fibre $Y_z$ is therefore a closed subscheme of $Y_\Omega$, and is proper over $\Omega$ by base change of the proper map $f_X$, and $Z$ is proper as a reduced closed component, using [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. It is also a component of $Y_\Omega$: it is a closed irreducible subset of this nodal one-dimensional curve and already has dimension one, so it is not a proper closed subset of an irreducible curve component. In particular it is contracted by $f_\Omega$ to $z$. If $Z$ met no other component, it would itself be a proper connected component. This is impossible by [lem-trf-no-isolated-contracted-fibre-component], whose hypotheses are exactly the flat pure-dimensional curves, proper generically isomorphic modification, smooth generic target and nodal source in the present assumptions. Hence at least one node on $Z$ joins it to a different component. Its branch on $\bar Z$ contributes at least one point to $B_Z$, so $n_Z\ge1$.

source.place: Theorem 1.1, proper contracted subcurve and boundary nodes. Here the fibre is over X, not the structural fibre over T.

proof.text: Put $g=g(\bar Z)$. If $g\ge2$, then $2g-2+n_Z\ge2$; if $g=1$, step 7 gives $2g-2+n_Z=n_Z\ge1$. Suppose $g=0$. By [lem-trf-genus-zero-smooth-proper-line], $\bar Z\cong\mathbf P^1_\Omega$. If $Z$ has a self-node, its two branches and the boundary branch from step 7 are distinct, so $n_Z\ge3$. If $Z$ has no self-node, it is smooth as an abstract component, and its normalization is an isomorphism by [lem-trf-nodal-normalization-adjunction]; thus $Z\cong\mathbf P^1_\Omega$. The given stability hypothesis now says that this contracted component has more than two distinct ambient singular or marked points. Since it has no self-nodes, each of those points has exactly one preimage on $\bar Z$, so again $n_Z\ge3$. In both genus-zero cases $2g-2+n_Z=n_Z-2\ge1$. Together with step 6 this proves strict positivity for every component specified in the item.

source.place: Theorem 1.1, stable pointed-subcurve computation; Stacks Tag 0C6U for the genus-zero characterization.

I checked every cited node's statement and the Stacks sources 0B6V, 0E2Y, 0C6U (8)⇒(1), 0C4D/0C4E and the 00SA/00SP/00SV/00SY/03H0 tags. Temkin's PDF is absent locally (WANTED is recorded and the proof is marked agent-written), so I checked that mathematics myself. The statement is unchanged and the definitions match the sibling Temkin nodes. Steps 1 and 3–8 are correct, and I checked the hypotheses of every lemma they apply. Step 7 is right that a rational point is closed, that the contracted 1-dimensional Z is a whole component, and that a component meeting nothing else would be a clopen proper contracted component. Step 8's genus cases (self-node gives 2 branches plus a separate boundary node; with no self-node, Z is P1 and stability gives at least 3 special points) are correct. Small cases: an exceptional P1 with one node is excluded by stability; with two marks it has degree 1; a genus-1 tail has degree 1; a rational self-nodal component has degree 1; the identity elliptic curve makes no claim. New nodes: all are true, self-contained, statement-only, unsplit, with correct blueprint.from/via and four kinds of search, and none duplicates an existing node. I proved no-isolated-contracted myself: Stein factorization plus upper semicontinuity of fibre dimension on V'=Spec f_*O_Y. The adjunction node holds because codimension c in a CM fibre gives relative regularity. Genus-zero is 0C6U (8)⇒(1). The normalization node is the classical branch-pole formula and cites the adjunction node in stmt_deps. None restates the item: the degree formula and positivity are proved in steps 5–8. lean.statement: theorem marked_nodal_dualizing_degrees (T : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral T] [IsNoetherian T] (C P : MultipointedCurve T) (η : T) (hη : IsGenericPoint η Set.univ) (hgenericCurve : Smooth (C.x.fiberToSpecResidueField η)) (hgenericMarking : Etale (C.d.fiberToSpecResidueField η)) (f : P.Hom C) (hstable : f.IsStable (T.fromSpecResidueField η)) : ∃ D : MarkedNodalDualizingDegreesData P, ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (z : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ C.X) (Z : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral Z] (j : Z ⟶ pullback f.curve z), IsClosedImmersion j → Set.range j ∈ irreducibleComponents (pullback (C := Scheme) f.curve z) → topologicalKrullDim Z = 1 → 0 < markedNodalComponentDegree Ω Z (j ≫ pullback.fst f.curve z) (j ≫ pullback.snd f.curve z) (markedNodalLine P D.omega)
